'''Alexander Borisovich Zamolodchikov''' ({{langx|ru|Алекса́ндр Бори́сович Замоло́дчиков}}; born September 18, 1952)  is a Russian-American theoretical physicist, known for his contributions to [[conformal field theory]], [[statistical mechanics]], [[string theory]] and [[condensed matter physics]].  

He is widely regarded as one of the most accomplished theoretical physicists<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |date=September 14, 2023 |title=Zamolodchikov Shares $3M Breakthrough Prize in Fundamental Physics |url=https://news.stonybrook.edu/university/zamolodchikov-shares-3m-breakthrough-prize-in-fundamental-physics/ |access-date=January 23, 2024 |language=en-US}}</ref> for his profound contributions to fundamental physics and especially to [[Quantum field theory|Quantum Field Theories]], for which he was awarded the [[Breakthrough Prize in Fundamental Physics]]<ref name=":0" /> in 2024. He is currently the [[C.N. Yang]] – Wei Deng Endowed Chair of Physics at [[Stony Brook University]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 23, 2017 |title=INTERNATIONALLY RENOWNED PHYSICIST APPOINTED AS CHEN NING YANG – WEI DENG ENDOWED CHAIR IN PHYSICS AND ASTRONOMY |url=https://www.stonybrook.edu/newsroom/general/2017-01-21-endowed-chair-in-physics-stony-brook.php/amp/ |access-date=September 14, 2023 |website=Stony Brook University}}</ref>

==Biography==
Born in [[Dubna|Novo-Ivankovo]], now part of [[Dubna]], Zamolodchikov earned a [[M.Sc.]] in [[nuclear engineering]] (1975) from [[Moscow Institute of Physics and Technology]], a [[Ph.D.]] in [[physics]] from the [[Institute for Theoretical and Experimental Physics]] (1978). He joined the research staff of [[Landau Institute for Theoretical Physics]] (1978) where he got a [[Doctor of Sciences]] degree (1983).

He co-authored the famous [[Belavin–Polyakov–Zamolodchikov equations|BPZ paper]] "Infinite Conformal Symmetry in Two-Dimensional Quantum Field Theory",<ref name=a>{{cite journal|author=Belavin AA|author-link=Alexander Belavin|author2=Polyakov AM|author2-link=Alexander Markovich Polyakov|author3=Zamolodchikov AB|title=Infinite conformal symmetry in two-dimensional quantum field theory|journal=Nucl. Phys. B|volume=241|issue=2|pages=333–80|date=1984|doi=10.1016/0550-3213(84)90052-X|bibcode = 1984NuPhB.241..333B |url=https://cds.cern.ch/record/152341}}</ref> with [[Alexander Markovich Polyakov|Alexander Polyakov]] and [[Alexander Belavin]].<ref name=a/><ref>{{cite journal|title=Princeton celebrates Polyakov's 60th|journal=CERN Courier|issue=March 1|pages=2|date=2006|url=http://cerncourier.com/cws/article/cern/29554/2|access-date=October 21, 2008|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110709210059/http://cerncourier.com/cws/article/cern/29554/2|archive-date=July 9, 2011|url-status=dead}}</ref>

He joined [[Rutgers University]] (1990) where he co-founded Rutgers New High Energy Theory Center, and was named Board of Governors Professor (2005).<ref>[http://news.rutgers.digitalwave.ws/medrel/news-releases/2005/04/alexander-zamolodchi-20050407 Alexander Zamolodchikov Named Board of Governors Professor of Physics] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161006054434/http://news.rutgers.digitalwave.ws/medrel/news-releases/2005/04/alexander-zamolodchi-20050407 |date=October 6, 2016 }}</ref>

In 2016, he became the inaugural holder of the [[C N Yang|C. N. Yang]]/Wei Deng Chair in the Department of Physics and Astronomy and C. N. Yang Institute for Theoretical Physics at [[Stony Brook University]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.physics.sunysb.edu/Physics/news/whatsnew_single.php?date=latest/20160825|title=Stony Brook Physics & Astronomy: News|website=www.physics.sunysb.edu|access-date=August 26, 2016}}</ref>

He is the twin brother of the late [[Alexei Zamolodchikov]] (1952–2007), also a noted physicist.<ref>[http://cerncourier.com/cws/article/cern/32529/4  Alexei Zamolodchikov 1952–2007] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180114185541/http://cerncourier.com/cws/article/cern/32529/4 |date=January 14, 2018 }} from [[CERN]] (January 1, 2008)</ref>

==Awards==
*1999: [[Dannie Heineman Prize for Mathematical Physics]] with [[Barry M. McCoy]] and [[Tai Tsun Wu]] for "their groundbreaking and penetrating work on classical statistical mechanics, integrable models and conformal field theories."
*2003/04: [[Humboldt Prize]]
*2005: [[Blaise Pascal Chair]] at the [[École Normale Supérieure]] in Paris
*2011: [[Lars Onsager Prize]], together with [[Alexander Belavin]] and [[Alexander Markovich Polyakov|Alexander Polyakov]], "for the remarkable ideas that they introduced concerning conformal field theory and soluble models of statistical mechanics in two dimensions."
*2011: [[Dirac Medal (ICTP)|Dirac Medal]] from the [[International Center for Theoretical Physics]], Trieste.
*2016: elected to the [[National Academy of Sciences]]<ref>{{citation|url=http://www.nasonline.org/news-and-multimedia/news/may-3-2016-NAS-Election.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160506052951/http://www.nasonline.org/news-and-multimedia/news/may-3-2016-NAS-Election.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=May 6, 2016|title=National Academy of Sciences Members and Foreign Associates Elected|department=News from the National Academy of Sciences|publisher=[[National Academy of Sciences]]|date=May 3, 2016|access-date=May 14, 2016}}.</ref>
*2024: [[Breakthrough Prize in Fundamental Physics]],<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 14, 2023 |title=BREAKTHROUGH PRIZE ANNOUNCES 2024 LAUREATES IN LIFE SCIENCES, FUNDAMENTAL PHYSICS, AND MATHEMATICS |url=https://breakthroughprize.org/News/83 |access-date=September 14, 2023 |website=Breakthrough Prize}}</ref> "for profound contributions to statistical physics and quantum field theory, with diverse and far-reaching applications in different branches of physics and mathematics."
